18.3: They shall discharge their duties to you and to the Tent as a whole, but they must not have any contact with the furnishings of the Shrine or with the altar, lest both they and you die.
18.4: They shall be attached to you and discharge the duties of the Tent of Meeting, all the service of the Tent; but no outsider shall intrude upon you
18.5: As you discharge the duties connected with the Shrine and the altar, that wrath may not again strike the Israelites.
18.6: I hereby take your fellow Levites from among the Israelites; they are assigned to you in dedication to GOD, to do the work of the Tent of Meeting
18.7: While you and your sons shall be careful to perform your priestly duties in everything pertaining to the altar and to what is behind the curtain. I make your priesthood a service of dedication; any outsider who encroaches shall be put to death.
18.8: GOD spoke further to Aaron: I hereby give you charge of My gifts, all the sacred donations of the Israelites; I grant them to you and to your sons as a perquisite, a due for all time.
18.9: This shall be yours from the most holy sacrifices, the offerings by fire: uncertain; lit. “from the fire.” every such offering that they render to Me as most holy sacrifices, namely, every grain offering, purgation offering, and reparation offering of theirs, shall belong to you and your sons.
18.10: You shall partake of them as most sacred donations: only males may eat them; you shall treat them as consecrated.
18.11: This, too, shall be yours: the gift offerings of their contributions, all the elevation offerings of the Israelites, I give to you and your wives, to your sons, and to the daughters that are with you, as a due for all time; everyone of your household who is pure may eat it.
18.12: All the best of the new oil, wine, and grain—the choice parts that they present to GOD—I give to you.
18.13: The first fruits of everything in their land, that they bring to GOD, shall be yours; everyone of your household who is pure may eat them.
18.14: Everything that has been proscribed in Israel shall be yours.
18.15: The first male issue of the womb of every being, human or animal, that is offered to GOD, shall be yours; but you shall have the first-born of human beings redeemed, and you shall also have the firstling of impure animals redeemed.
18.16: Take as their redemption price, from the age of one month up, the money equivalent of five shekels by the sanctuary weight, which is twenty gerahs.
18.17: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.
18.18: But their meat shall be yours: it shall be yours like the breast of elevation offering and like the right thigh.
18.19: All the sacred gifts that the Israelites set aside for GOD I give to you, to your sons, and to the daughters that are with you, as a due for all time. It shall be an everlasting covenant of salt before GOD for you and for your offspring as well.
18.20: And GOD said to Aaron: You shall, however, have no territorial share among them or own any portion in their midst; I am your portion and your share among the Israelites.
18.21: And to the Levites I hereby give all the tithes in Israel as their share in return for the services that they perform, the services of the Tent of Meeting.
18.22: Henceforth, Israelites shall not trespass on the Tent of Meeting, and thus incur guilt and die
18.23: Only Levites shall perform the services of the Tent of Meeting; others would incur guilt. It is the law for all time throughout the ages. But they shall have no territorial share among the Israelites
18.24: For it is the tithes set aside by the Israelites as a gift to GOD that I give to the Levites as their share. Therefore I have said concerning them: They shall have no territorial share among the Israelites.
18.26: Speak to the Levites and say to them: When you receive from the Israelites their tithes, which I have assigned to you as your share, you shall set aside from them one-tenth of the tithe as a gift to GOD.
18.27: This shall be accounted to you as your gift. As with the new grain from the threshing floor or the flow from the vat
18.28: So shall you on your part set aside a gift for GOD from all the tithes that you receive from the Israelites; and from them you shall bring the gift for GOD to Aaron the priest.
18.29: You shall set aside all gifts due to GOD from everything that is donated to you, from each thing its best portion, the part thereof that is to be consecrated.
18.30: Say to them further: When you have removed the best part from it, you Levites may consider it the same as the yield of threshing floor or vat.
18.31: You and your households may eat it anywhere, for it is your recompense for your services in the Tent of Meeting.
18.32: You will incur no guilt through it, once you have removed the best part from it; but you must not profane the sacred donations of the Israelites, lest you die.

19.1: GOD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying
19.2: This is the ritual law that GOD has commanded: Instruct the Israelite people to bring you a red cow without blemish, in which there is no defect and on which no yoke has been laid.
19.3: You shall give it to Eleazar the priest. It shall be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
19.4: Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
19.5: The cow shall be burned in his sight—its hide, flesh, and blood shall be burned, its dung included
19.6: And the priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and crimson stuff, and throw them into the fire consuming the cow.
19.7: The priest shall wash his garments and bathe in water; after that the priest may reenter the camp, but he shall be impure until evening.
19.8: The one who performed the burning shall also wash their garments in water, bathe, and be impure until evening.
19.9: Someone else who is pure shall gather up the ashes of the cow and deposit them outside the camp in a pure place, to be kept for water of lustration for the Israelite community. It is for purgation.
19.10: The one who gathers up the ashes of the cow shall also wash their clothes and be impure until evening. This shall be a permanent law for the Israelites and for the strangers who reside among them.
19.11: Anyone who touches the corpse of any human being shall be impure for seven days.
19.12: They shall undergo cleansing with the ashes on the third day and on the seventh day, and then be pure; if they fail to undergo cleansing on the third and seventh days, they shall not be pure.
19.13: Whoever touches a corpse—the body of a person who has died—and does not undergo cleansing, defiles GOD’s Tabernacle; that person shall be cut off from Israel. Since the water of lustration was not dashed on them, they remain impure; their impurity is still upon them.
19.14: This is the ritual: When a person dies in a tent, whoever enters the tent and whoever is in the tent shall be impure seven days
19.15: And every open vessel, with no lid fastened down, shall be impure.
19.16: And in the open, anyone who touches a person who was killed or who died naturally, or human bone, or a grave, shall be impure seven days.
19.17: Some of the ashes from the fire of purgation shall be taken for the impure person, and fresh water shall be added to them in a vessel.
19.18: Then someone who is pure shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle on the tent and on all the vessels and people who were there, or on the one who touched the bones or the person who was killed or died naturally or the grave.
19.19: The pure person shall sprinkle it upon the impure person on the third day and on the seventh day, thus cleansing that person by the seventh day. The latter shall then wash their clothes and bathe in water—and at nightfall shall be pure.
19.20: If anyone who has become impure fails to undergo cleansing, that person shall be cut off from the congregation for having defiled GOD’s sanctuary. The water of lustration was not dashed on them—they are impure.
19.21: That shall be for them a law for all time. Further, whoever sprinkled the water of lustration shall wash their clothes; and whoever touches the water of lustration shall be impure until evening.
19.22: Whatever that impure person touches shall be impure; and the person who touches that impure one shall be impure until evening.

20.1: The Israelites arrived in a body at the wilderness of Zin on the first new moon, and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
20.2: The community was without water, and they joined against Moses and Aaron.
20.3: The people quarreled with Moses, saying, “If only we had perished when our brothers perished by GOD’s will!
20.4: Why have you brought GOD’s congregation into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die there?
20.5: Why did you make us leave Egypt to bring us to this wretched place, a place with no grain or figs or vines or pomegranates? There is not even water to drink!”
20.6: Moses and Aaron came away from the congregation to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and fell on their faces. The Presence of GOD appeared to them
20.7: And GOD spoke to Moses, saying
20.8: “You and your brother Aaron take the rod and assemble the community, and before their very eyes order the rock to yield its water. Thus you shall produce water for them from the rock and provide drink for the congregation and their livestock.”
20.9: Moses took the rod from before GOD, as he had been commanded.
20.10: Moses and Aaron assembled the congregation in front of the rock; and he said to them, “Listen, you rebels, shall we get water for you out of this rock?”
20.11: And Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his rod. Out came copious water, and the community and their livestock drank.
20.12: But GOD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust Me enough to affirm My sanctity in the sight of the Israelite people, therefore you shall not lead this congregation into the land that I have given them.”
20.13: Those are the waters of Meribah—meaning that the Israelites quarrelled with GOD—whose sanctity was affirmed through them.
20.14: From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom: “Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the hardships that have befallen us
20.15: That our ancestors went down to Egypt, that we dwelt in Egypt a long time, and that the Egyptians dealt harshly with us and our ancestors.
20.16: We cried to GOD—who, upon hearing our plea, sent a messenger who freed us from Egypt. Now we are in Kadesh, the town on the border of your territory.
20.17: Allow us, then, to cross your country. We will not pass through fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from wells. We will follow the king’s highway, turning off neither to the right nor to the left until we have crossed your territory.”
20.18: But Edom answered him, “You shall not pass through us, else we will go out against you with the sword.”
20.19: “We will keep to the beaten track,” the Israelites said to them, “and if we or our cattle drink your water, we will pay for it. We ask only for passage on foot—it is but a small matter.”
20.20: But they replied, “You shall not pass through!” And Edom went out against them in heavy force, strongly armed.
20.21: So Edom would not let Israel cross their territory, and Israel turned away from them.
20.22: Setting out from Kadesh, the Israelites arrived in a body at Mount Hor.
20.23: At Mount Hor, on the boundary of the land of Edom, GOD said to Moses and Aaron
20.24: “Let Aaron be gathered to his kin: he is not to enter the land that I have assigned to the Israelite people, because you disobeyed My command about the waters of Meribah.
20.25: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up on Mount Hor.
20.26: Strip Aaron of his vestments and put them on his son Eleazar. There Aaron shall be gathered unto the dead.”
20.27: Moses did as GOD had commanded. They ascended Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
20.28: Moses stripped Aaron of his vestments and put them on his son Eleazar, and Aaron died there on the summit of the mountain. When Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain
20.29: The whole community knew that Aaron had breathed his last. All the house of Israel bewailed Aaron thirty days.

21.1: When the Canaanite, king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negeb, learned that Israel was coming by the way of Atharim, uncertain. Targum and other ancient versions render “the way taken by the scouts.” he engaged Israel in battle and took some of them captive.
21.2: Then Israel made a vow to GOD and said, “If You deliver this people into our hand, we will proscribe their towns.”
21.3: GOD heeded Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites; and they and their cities were proscribed. So that place was named Hormah. “to proscribe.”
21.4: They set out from Mount Hor by way of the Sea of Reeds to skirt the land of Edom. But the people grew restive on the journey
21.5: And the people spoke against God and against Moses, “Why did you make us leave Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and no water, and we have come to loathe this miserable food.”
21.6: GOD sent seraph uncertain. serpents against the people. They bit the people and many of the Israelites died.
21.7: The people came to Moses and said, “We sinned by speaking against GOD and against you. Intercede with GOD to take away the serpents from us!” And Moses interceded for the people.
21.8: Then GOD said to Moses, “Make a seraph figure and mount it on a standard. And anyone who was bitten who then looks at it shall recover.”
21.9: Moses made a copper serpent and mounted it on a standard; and if someone was bitten by a serpent, they would look at the copper serpent and recover.
21.10: The Israelites marched on and encamped at Oboth.
21.11: They set out from Oboth and encamped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness bordering on Moab to the east.
21.12: From there they set out and encamped at the wadi Zered.
21.13: From there they set out and encamped beyond the Arnon, that is, in the wilderness that extends from the territory of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the boundary of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
21.14: Therefore the Book of the Wars of GOD speaks of “…Waheb in Suphah, and the wadis: the Arnon
21.15: With its tributary wadis, stretched along the settled country of Ar, hugging the territory of Moab…”
21.16: And from there to Beer, which is the well where GOD said to Moses, “Assemble the people that I may give them water.”
21.17: Then Israel sang this song: Spring up, O well—sing to it
21.18: The well that the chieftains dug, That the nobles of the people started With maces, with their own staffs. And from Midbar to Mattanah
21.19: And from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth
21.20: And from Bamoth to the valley that is in the country of Moab, at the peak of Pisgah, overlooking the wasteland.
21.21: Israel now sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying
21.22: “Let me pass through your country. We will not turn off into fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from wells. We will follow the king’s highway until we have crossed your territory.”
21.23: But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his troops and went out against Israel in the wilderness. He came to Jahaz and engaged Israel in battle.
21.24: But Israel put them to the sword, and took possession of their land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as Az of the Ammonites, for Az marked the boundary of the Ammonites.
21.25: Israel took all those towns. And Israel settled in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its dependencies.
21.26: Now Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against a former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
21.27: Therefore the bards would recite: “Come to Heshbon; firmly built And well founded is Sihon’s city.
21.28: For fire went forth from Heshbon, Flame from Sihon’s city, Consuming Ar of Moab, The lords of Bamoth by the Arnon.
21.29: Woe to you, O Moab! You are undone, O people of Chemosh! His sons are rendered fugitive And his daughters captive By an Amorite king, Sihon.”
21.30: Yet we have cast them down utterly, Heshbon along with Dibon; We have wrought desolation at Nophah, Which is hard by Medeba.
21.31: So Israel occupied the land of the Amorites.
21.32: Then Moses sent to spy out Jazer, and they captured its dependencies and dispossessed the Amorites who were there.
21.33: They marched on and went up the road to Bashan, and King Og of Bashan, with all his troops, came out to Edrei to engage them in battle.
21.34: But GOD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I give him and all his troops and his land into your hand. You shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites who dwelt in Heshbon.”
21.35: They defeated him and his sons and all his troops, until no remnant was left him; and they took possession of his country.

22.1: The Israelites then marched on and encamped in the steppes of Moab, across the Jordan from Jericho.
22.2: Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
22.3: Moab was alarmed because that people was so numerous. Moab dreaded the Israelites
22.4: And Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this horde will lick clean all that is about us as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” Balak son of Zippor, who was king of Moab at that time
22.5: Sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor in Pethor, which is by the Euphrates, in the land of his kinsfolk, to invite him, saying, “There is a people that came out of Egypt; it hides the earth from view, and it is settled next to me.
22.6: Come then, put a curse upon this people for me, since they are too numerous for me; perhaps I can thus defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that whomever you bless is blessed indeed, and whomever you curse is cursed.”
22.7: The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian, versed in divination, set out. They came to Balaam and gave him Balak’s message.
22.8: He said to them, “Spend the night here, and I shall reply to you as GOD may instruct me.” So the Moabite dignitaries stayed with Balaam.
22.9: God came to Balaam and said, “What do these men want of you?”
22.10: Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message
22.11: Here is a people that came out from Egypt and hides the earth from view. Come now and curse them for me; perhaps I can engage them in battle and drive them off.”
22.12: But God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. You must not curse that people, for they are blessed.”
22.13: Balaam arose in the morning and said to Balak’s dignitaries, “Go back to your own country, for GOD will not let me go with you.”
22.14: The Moabite dignitaries left, and they came to Balak and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
22.15: Then Balak sent other dignitaries, more numerous and distinguished than the first.
22.16: They came to Balaam and said to him, “Thus says Balak son of Zippor: Please do not refuse to come to me.
22.17: I will reward you richly and I will do anything you ask of me. Only come and damn this people for me.”
22.18: Balaam replied to Balak’s officials, “Though Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything, big or little, contrary to the command of the ETERNAL my God.
22.19: So you, too, stay here overnight, and let me find out what else GOD may say to me.”
22.20: That night God came to Balaam and said to him, “If the men have come to invite you, you may go with them. But whatever I command you, that you shall do.”
22.21: When he arose in the morning, Balaam saddled his jenny and departed with the Moabite dignitaries.
22.22: But God was incensed at his going; so an angel of GOD took a position in his way as an adversary. He was riding on his jenny, with his two servants alongside
22.23: When the jenny caught sight of the angel of GOD standing in the way, with his drawn sword in his hand. The jenny swerved from the road and went into the fields; and Balaam beat the jenny to turn her back onto the road.
22.24: The angel of GOD then stationed himself in a lane between the vineyards, with a fence on either side.
22.25: The jenny, seeing the angel of GOD, pressed herself against the wall and squeezed Balaam’s foot against the wall; so he beat her again.
22.26: Once more the angel of GOD moved forward and stationed himself on a spot so narrow that there was no room to swerve right or left.
22.27: When the jenny now saw the angel of GOD, she lay down under Balaam; and Balaam was furious and beat the jenny with his stick.
22.28: Then GOD opened the jenny’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
22.29: Balaam said to the jenny, “You have made a mockery of me! If I had a sword with me, I’d kill you.”
22.30: The jenny said to Balaam, “Look, I am the jenny that you have been riding all along until this day! Have I been in the habit of doing thus to you?” And he answered, “No.”
22.31: Then GOD uncovered Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of GOD standing in the way, his drawn sword in his hand; thereupon he bowed right down to the ground.
22.32: The angel of GOD said to him, “Why have you beaten your jenny these three times? It is I who came out as an adversary, for the errand is obnoxious uncertain. to me.
22.33: And when the jenny saw me, she shied away because of me those three times. If she had not shied away from me, you are the one I should have killed, while sparing her.”
22.34: Balaam said to the angel of GOD, “I erred because I did not know that you were standing in my way. If you still disapprove, I will turn back.”
22.35: But the angel of GOD said to Balaam, “Go with the men. But you must say nothing except what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak’s dignitaries.
22.36: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at Ir-moab, which is on the Arnon border, at its farthest point.
22.37: Balak said to Balaam, “When I first sent to invite you, why didn’t you come to me? Am I really unable to reward you?”
22.38: But Balaam said to Balak, “And now that I have come to you, have I the power to speak freely? I can utter only the word that God puts into my mouth.”
22.39: Balaam went with Balak and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
22.40: Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and had them served to Balaam and the dignitaries with him.
22.41: In the morning Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see a portion of the people.

23.1: Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here and have seven bulls and seven rams ready here for me.”
23.2: Balak did as Balaam directed; and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.
23.3: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your offerings while I am gone. Perhaps GOD will grant me a manifestation, and whatever is revealed to me I will tell you.” And he went off alone. uncertain.
23.4: God became manifest to Balaam, who stated, “I have set up the seven altars and offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.”
23.5: And GOD put a word in Balaam’s mouth and said, “Return to Balak and speak thus.”
23.6: So he returned to him and found him standing beside his offerings, and all the Moabite dignitaries with him.
23.7: He took up his theme, and said: From Aram has Balak brought me, Moab’s king from the hills of the East: Come, curse me Jacob, Come, tell Israel’s doom!
23.8: How can I damn whom God, as often in these poems. has not damned, How doom when GOD has not doomed?
23.9: As I see them from the mountain tops, Gaze on them from the heights, There is a people that dwells apart, Not reckoned among the nations
23.10: Who can count the dust of Jacob, Number the dust-cloud of Israel? May I die the death of the upright, a play on yeshurun (“Jeshurun” in Deut. 32.15), a name for Israel. May my fate be like theirs!
23.11: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? Here I brought you to damn my enemies, and instead you have blessed them!”
23.12: He replied, “I can only repeat faithfully what GOD puts in my mouth.”
23.13: Then Balak said to him, “Come with me to another place from which you can see them—you will see only a portion of them; you will not see all of them—and damn them for me from there.”
23.14: With that, he took him to Sedeh-zophim, on the summit of Pisgah. He built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
23.15: And Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your offerings, while I seek a manifestation yonder.”
23.16: GOD became manifest to Balaam and put a word in his mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and speak thus.”
23.17: He went to him and found him standing beside his offerings, and the Moabite dignitaries with him. Balak asked him, “What did GOD say?”
23.18: And he took up his theme, and said: Up, Balak, attend, Give ear unto me, son of Zippor!
23.19: God is not human to be capricious, Or mortal to have a change of heart. Would God speak and not act, Promise and not fulfill?
23.20: My message was to bless: When God blesses, I cannot reverse it.
23.21: No harm is in sight for Jacob, No woe in view for Israel. The ETERNAL their God is with them, And their Sovereign’s acclaim in their midst.
23.22: God who freed them from Egypt Is for them like the horns of the wild ox.
23.23: Lo, there is no augury in Jacob, No divining in Israel: Jacob is told at once, Yea Israel, what God has planned.
23.24: Lo, a people that rises like a lioness, uncertain. Leaps up like a lion, Rests not till it has feasted on prey And drunk the blood of the slain.
23.25: Thereupon Balak said to Balaam, “Don’t curse them and don’t bless them!”
23.26: In reply, Balaam said to Balak, “But I told you: Whatever GOD says, that I must do.”
23.27: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place. Perhaps God will deem it right that you damn them for me there.”
23.28: Balak took Balaam to the peak of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
23.29: Balaam said to Balak, “Build me here seven altars, and have seven bulls and seven rams ready for me here.”
23.30: Balak did as Balaam said: he offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.

24.1: Now Balaam, seeing that it pleased GOD to bless Israel, did not, as on previous occasions, go in search of omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness.
24.2: As Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the spirit of God came upon him.
24.3: Taking up his theme, he said: Word of Balaam son of Beor, Word of the man; more precisely, a man who makes his presence felt. whose eye is true
24.4: Word of one who hears God’s speech, Who beholds visions from the Almighty, Prostrate, but with eyes unveiled
24.5: How fair are your tents, O Jacob, Your dwellings, O Israel!
24.6: Like palm-groves that stretch out, Like gardens beside a river, Like aloes planted by GOD, Like cedars beside the water
24.7: Their boughs drip with moisture, Their roots have abundant water. Their ruler shall rise above Agag, Their sovereignty shall be exalted.
24.8: God who freed them from Egypt Is for them like the horns of the wild ox. They shall devour enemy nations, Crush their bones, And smash their arrows.
24.9: They crouch, they lie down like a lion, Like a lioness; who dares rouse them? Blessed are they who bless you, Accursed they who curse you!
24.10: Enraged at Balaam, Balak struck his hands together. “I called you,” Balak said to Balaam, “to damn my enemies, and instead you have blessed them these three times!
24.11: Back with you at once to your own place! I was going to reward you richly, but GOD has denied you the reward.”
24.12: Balaam replied to Balak, “But I even told the messengers you sent to me
24.13: ‘Though Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not of my own accord do anything good or bad contrary to GOD’s command. What GOD says, that I must say.’
24.14: And now, as I go back to my people, let me inform you of what this people will do to your people in days to come.”
24.15: He took up his theme, and said: Word of Balaam son of Beor, Word of the man whose eye is true
24.16: Word of one who hears God’s speech, Who obtains knowledge from the Most High, And beholds visions from the Almighty, Prostrate, but with eyes unveiled
24.17: What I see for them is not yet, What I behold will not be soon: A star rises from Jacob, A scepter comes forth from Israel; It smashes the brow of Moab, The foundation of all children of Seth.
24.18: Edom becomes a possession, Yea, Seir a possession of its enemies; But Israel is triumphant.
24.19: A victor issues from Jacob To wipe out what is left of Ir.
24.20: He saw Amalek and, taking up his theme, he said: A leading nation is Amalek; But its fate is to perish forever.
24.21: He saw the Kenites and, taking up his theme, he said: Though your abode be secure, And your nest be set among cliffs
24.22: Yet shall Kain be consumed, When Asshur takes you captive.
24.23: He took up his theme and said: Alas, who can survive except God has willed it!
24.24: Ships come from the quarter of Kittim; They subject Asshur, subject Eber. They, too, shall perish forever.
24.25: Then Balaam set out on his journey back home; and Balak also went his way.

25.1: While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people profaned themselves by whoring with the Moabite women
25.2: Who invited the people to the sacrifices for their god. The people partook of them and worshiped that god.
25.3: Thus Israel attached itself to Baal-peor, and GOD was incensed with Israel.
25.4: GOD said to Moses, “Take all the ringleaders and have them publicly impaled before GOD, so that GOD’s wrath may turn away from Israel.”
25.5: So Moses said to Israel’s officials, “Each of you slay those of your men who attached themselves to Baal-peor.”
25.6: Just then a certain Israelite man came and brought a Midianite woman over to his companions, in the sight of Moses and of the whole Israelite community who were weeping at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
25.7: When Phinehas, son of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he left the assembly and, taking a spear in his hand
25.8: He followed the Israelite man into the chamber and stabbed both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through the belly. Then the plague against the Israelites was checked.
25.9: Those who died of the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
25.11: “Phinehas, son of Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, has turned back My wrath from the Israelites by displaying among them his passion for Me, so that I did not wipe out the Israelite people in My passion.
25.12: Say, therefore, ‘I grant him My pact of friendship.
25.13: It shall be for him and his descendants after him a pact of priesthood for all time, because he took impassioned action for his God, thus making expiation for the Israelites.’”
25.14: The name of the Israelite man who was killed, the one who was killed with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, chieftain of a Simeonite ancestral house.
25.15: The name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur; he was the tribal head of an ancestral house in Midian.
25.18: For they assailed you by the trickery they practiced against you—because of the affair of Peor and because of the affair of their kinswoman Cozbi, daughter of the Midianite chieftain, who was killed at the time of the plague on account of Peor.”

26.1: When the plague was over, GOD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest
26.2: “Take a census of the whole Israelite community from the age of twenty years up, by their ancestral houses, all Israelites able to bear arms.”
26.3: So Moses and Eleazar the priest, on the steppes of Moab, at the Jordan near Jericho, gave instructions about them, namely
26.4: Those from twenty years up, as GOD had commanded Moses. The descendants of the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt were
26.5: Reuben, Israel’s first-born. Descendants of Reuben: Of Enoch, the clan of the Enochites; of Pallu, the clan of the Palluites
26.6: Of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
26.7: Those are the clans of the Reubenites. The men enrolled came to 43,730.
26.9: The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, and Dathan and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram, chosen in the assembly, who agitated against Moses and Aaron as part of Korah’s band when they agitated against GOD.
26.10: Whereupon the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up with Korah—when that band died, when the fire consumed the two hundred and fifty men—and they became an example.
26.11: The sons of Korah, however, did not die.
26.12: Descendants of Simeon by their clans: Of Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites
26.13: Of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; of Saul, the clan of the Saulites.
26.14: Those are the clans of the Simeonites; men enrolled: 22,200.
26.15: Descendants of Gad by their clans: Of Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; of Shuni, the clan of the Shunites
26.16: Of Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; of Eri, the clan of the Erites
26.17: Of Arod, the clan of the Arodites; of Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
26.18: Those are the clans of Gad’s descendants; men enrolled: 40,500.
26.19: Born to Judah: Er and Onan. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
26.20: Descendants of Judah by their clans: Of Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; of Perez, the clan of the Perezites; of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
26.21: Descendants of Perez: of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
26.22: Those are the clans of Judah; men enrolled: 76,500.
26.23: Descendants of Issachar by their clans: Of Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the clan of the Punites
26.24: Of Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
26.25: Those are the clans of Issachar; men enrolled: 64,300.
26.26: Descendants of Zebulun by their clans: Of Sered, the clan of the Seredites; of Elon, the clan of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
26.27: Those are the clans of the Zebulunites; men enrolled: 60,500.
26.28: The sons of Joseph were Manasseh and Ephraim—by their clans.
26.29: Descendants of Manasseh: Of Machir, the clan of the Machirites.—Machir begot Gilead.—Of Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
26.30: These were the descendants of Gilead: Of Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; of Helek, the clan of the Helekites
26.31: Of Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; of Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites
26.32: Of Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; of Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
26.33: Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. The names of Zelophehad’s daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
26.34: Those are the clans of Manasseh; men enrolled: 52,700.
26.35: These are the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: Of Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the clan of the Becherites; of Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
26.36: These are the descendants of Shuthelah: Of Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
26.37: Those are the clans of Ephraim’s descendants; men enrolled: 32,500. Those are the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
26.38: The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: Of Bela, the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites
26.39: Of Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
26.40: The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: Of Ard, the clan of the Ardites; of Naaman, the clan of the Naamanites.
26.41: Those are the descendants of Benjamin by their clans; men enrolled: 45,600.
26.42: These are the descendants of Dan by their clans: Of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. Those are the clans of Dan, by their clans.
26.43: All the clans of the Shuhamites; men enrolled: 64,400.
26.44: Descendants of Asher by their clans: Of Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
26.45: Of the descendants of Beriah: Of Heber, the clan of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
26.46: The name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
26.47: These are the clans of Asher’s descendants; men enrolled: 53,400.
26.48: Descendants of Naphtali by their clans: Of Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the clan of the Gunites
26.49: Of Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
26.50: Those are the clans of the Naphtalites, clan by clan; men enrolled: 45,400.
26.51: This is the enrollment of the Israelites: 601,730.
26.53: “Among these shall the land be apportioned as shares, according to the listed names
26.54: With larger groups increase the share, with smaller groups reduce the share. Each is to be assigned its share according to its enrollment.
26.55: The land, moreover, is to be apportioned by lot; and the allotment shall be made according to the listings of their ancestral tribes.
26.56: Each portion shall be assigned by lot, whether for larger or smaller groups.”
26.57: This is the enrollment of the Levites by their clans: Of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; of Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
26.58: These are the clans of Levi: The clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites.—Kohath begot Amram.
26.59: The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt; she bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam.
26.60: To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
26.61: Nadab and Abihu died when they offered alien fire before GOD.
26.62: Their enrollment of 23,000 comprised all males from a month up. They were not part of the regular enrollment of the Israelites, since no share was assigned to them among the Israelites.
26.63: These are the ones enrolled by Moses and Eleazar the priest who registered the Israelites on the steppes of Moab, at the Jordan near Jericho.
26.64: Among these there was not one of those enrolled by Moses and Aaron the priest when they recorded the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
26.65: For GOD had said of them, “They shall die in the wilderness.” Not one of them survived, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

27.1: The daughters of Zelophehad, of Manassite family—son of Hepher son of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh son of Joseph—came forward. The names of the daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
27.2: They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the chieftains, and the whole assembly, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and they said
27.3: “Our father died in the wilderness. He was not one of the faction, Korah’s faction, that banded together against GOD, but died for his own sin; and he has left no sons.
27.4: Let not our father’s name be lost to his clan just because he had no son! Give us a holding among our father’s kinsmen!”
27.5: Moses brought their case before GOD.
27.7: “The plea of Zelophehad’s daughters is just: you should give them a hereditary holding among their father’s kinsmen; transfer their father’s share to them.
27.8: “Further, speak to the Israelite people as follows: ‘If a man dies without leaving a son, you shall transfer his property to his daughter.
27.9: If he has no daughter, you shall assign his property to his brothers.
27.10: If he has no brothers, you shall assign his property to his father’s brothers.
27.11: If his father had no brothers, you shall assign his property to his nearest relative in his own clan, who shall inherit it.’ This shall be the law of procedure for the Israelites, in accordance with GOD’s command to Moses.”
27.12: GOD said to Moses, “Ascend these heights of Abarim and view the land that I have given to the Israelite people.
27.13: When you have seen it, you too shall be gathered to your kin, just as your brother Aaron was.
27.14: For, in the wilderness of Zin, when the community was contentious, you disobeyed My command to uphold My sanctity in their sight by means of the water.” Those are the waters of Meribath-kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.
27.16: “Let GOD, Source of the breath of all flesh, appoint someone over the community
27.17: Who shall go out before them and come in before them, and who shall take them out and bring them in, so that GOD’s community may not be like sheep that have no shepherd.”
27.18: And GOD answered Moses, “Single out Joshua son of Nun, an inspired man, and lay your hand upon him.
27.19: Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community, and commission him in their sight.
27.20: Invest him with some of your authority, so that the whole Israelite community may obey.
27.21: But he shall present himself to Eleazar the priest, who shall on his behalf seek the decision of the Urim before GOD. By such instruction they shall go out and by such instruction they shall come in, he and all the Israelites, and the whole community.”
27.22: Moses did as GOD commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community.
27.23: He laid his hands upon him and commissioned him—as GOD had spoken through Moses.

28.2: Command the Israelite people and say to them: Be punctilious in presenting to Me at stated times the offerings of food due Me, as offerings by fire of pleasing odor to Me.
28.3: Say to them: These are the offerings by fire that you are to present to GOD: As a regular burnt offering every day, two yearling lambs without blemish.
28.4: You shall offer one lamb in the morning, and the other lamb you shall offer at twilight.
28.5: And as a grain offering, there shall be a tenth of an ephah of choice flour with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil mixed in
28.6: The regular burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD.
28.7: The libation with it shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb, to be poured in the sacred precinct as an offering of fermented drink to GOD.
28.8: The other lamb you shall offer at twilight, preparing the same grain offering and libation as in the morning—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD.
28.9: On the sabbath day: two yearling lambs without blemish, together with two-tenths of a measure. of choice flour with oil mixed in as a grain offering, and with the proper libation
28.10: A burnt offering for every sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its libation.
28.11: On your new moons you shall present a burnt offering to GOD: two bulls of the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, without blemish.
28.12: As grain offering for each bull: three-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in. As grain offering for each ram: two-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in.
28.13: As grain offering for each lamb: a tenth of a measure of fine flour with oil mixed in. Such shall be the burnt offering of pleasing odor, an offering by fire to GOD.
28.14: Their libations shall be: half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. That shall be the monthly burnt offering for each new moon of the year.
28.15: And there shall be one goat as a purgation offering to GOD, to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its libation.
28.16: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, there shall be a passover sacrifice to GOD
28.17: And on the fifteenth day of that month a festival. Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days.
28.18: The first day shall be a sacred occasion: you shall not work at your occupations.
28.19: You shall present an offering by fire, a burnt offering, to GOD: two bulls of the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs—see that they are without blemish.
28.20: The grain offering with them shall be of choice flour with oil mixed in: prepare three-tenths of a measure for a bull, two-tenths for a ram
28.21: And for each of the seven lambs prepare one-tenth of a measure.
28.22: And there shall be one goat for a purgation offering, to make expiation in your behalf.
28.23: You shall present these in addition to the morning portion of the regular burnt offering.
28.24: You shall offer the like daily for seven days as food, an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD; they shall be offered, with their libations, in addition to the regular burnt offering.
28.25: And the seventh day shall be a sacred occasion for you: you shall not work at your occupations.
28.26: On the day of the first fruits, your Feast of Weeks, when you bring an offering of new grain to GOD, you shall observe a sacred occasion: you shall not work at your occupations.
28.27: You shall present a burnt offering of pleasing odor to GOD: two bulls of the herd, one ram, seven yearling lambs.
28.28: The grain offering with them shall be of choice flour with oil mixed in, three-tenths of a measure for a bull, two-tenths for a ram
28.29: And one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
28.30: And there shall be one goat for expiation in your behalf.
28.31: You shall present them—see that they are without blemish—with their libations, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering.

29.1: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall observe a sacred occasion: you shall not work at your occupations. You shall observe it as a day when the horn is sounded.
29.2: You shall present a burnt offering of pleasing odor to GOD: one bull of the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, without blemish.
29.3: The grain offering with them—choice flour with oil mixed in—shall be: three-tenths of a measure for a bull, two-tenths for a ram
29.4: And one-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
29.5: And there shall be one goat for a purgation offering, to make expiation in your behalf
29.6: In addition to the burnt offering of the new moon with its grain offering and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, each with its libation as prescribed, offerings by fire of pleasing odor to GOD.
29.7: On the tenth day of the same seventh month you shall observe a sacred occasion when you shall practice self-denial. You shall do no work.
29.8: You shall present to GOD a burnt offering of pleasing odor: one bull of the herd, one ram, seven yearling lambs; see that they are without blemish.
29.9: The grain offering with them—of choice flour with oil mixed in—shall be: three-tenths of a measure for a bull, two-tenths for the one ram
29.10: One-tenth for each of the seven lambs.
29.11: And there shall be one goat for a purgation offering, in addition to the purgation offering of expiation and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering, each with its libation.
29.12: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you shall observe a sacred occasion: you shall not work at your occupations.—Seven days you shall observe a festival of GOD.
29.13: You shall present a burnt offering, an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD: Thirteen bulls of the herd, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs; they shall be without blemish.
29.14: The grain offerings with them—of choice flour with oil mixed in—shall be: three-tenths of a measure for each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths for each of the two rams
29.15: And one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs.
29.16: And there shall be one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libation.
29.17: Second day: Twelve bulls of the herd, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs, without blemish
29.18: The grain offerings and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.19: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libations.
29.20: Third day: Eleven bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs, without blemish
29.21: The grain offerings and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.22: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libation.
29.23: Fourth day: Ten bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs, without blemish
29.24: The grain offerings and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.25: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libation.
29.26: Fifth day: Nine bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs, without blemish
29.27: The grain offerings and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.28: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libation.
29.29: Sixth day: Eight bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs, without blemish
29.30: The grain offerings and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.31: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libations.
29.32: Seventh day: Seven bulls, two rams, fourteen yearling lambs, without blemish
29.33: The grain offerings and libations for the bulls, rams, and lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.34: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libation.
29.35: On the eighth day you shall hold a solemn gathering; uncertain. Cf. Lev. 23.36; Deut. 16.8. you shall not work at your occupations.
29.36: You shall present a burnt offering, an offering by fire of pleasing odor to GOD; one bull, one ram, seven yearling lambs, without blemish
29.37: The grain offerings and libations for the bull, the ram, and the lambs, in the quantities prescribed
29.38: And one goat for a purgation offering—in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and libation.
29.39: All these you shall offer to GOD at the stated times, in addition to your votive and freewill offerings, be they burnt offerings, grain offerings, libations, or offerings of well-being.

30.1: So Moses spoke to the Israelites just as GOD had commanded Moses.
30.2: Moses spoke to the heads of the Israelite tribes, saying: This is what GOD has commanded
30.3: If anyone makes a vow to GOD or takes an oath imposing an obligation on themselves, they shall not break their pledge; they must carry out all that has crossed their lips.
30.4: If a woman makes a vow to GOD or assumes an obligation while still in her father’s household by reason of her youth
30.5: And her father learns of her vow or her self-imposed obligation and offers no objection, all her vows shall stand and every self-imposed obligation shall stand.
30.6: But if her father restrains her on the day he finds out, none of her vows or self-imposed obligations shall stand; and GOD will forgive her, since her father restrained her.
30.7: If she should become someone’s wife while her vow or the commitment to which she bound herself is still in force
30.8: And her husband learns of it and offers no objection on the day he finds out, her vows shall stand and her self-imposed obligations shall stand.
30.9: But if her husband restrains her on the day that he learns of it, he thereby annuls her vow that was in force or the commitment to which she bound herself; and GOD will forgive her.
30.10: The vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, however, whatever she has imposed on herself, shall be binding upon her.
30.11: So, too, if, while in her husband’s household, she makes a vow or imposes an obligation on herself by oath
30.12: And her husband learns of it, yet offers no objection—thus failing to restrain her—all her vows shall stand and all her self-imposed obligations shall stand.
30.13: But if her husband does annul them on the day he finds out, then nothing that has crossed her lips shall stand, whether vows or self-imposed obligations. Her husband has annulled them, and GOD will forgive her.
30.14: Every vow and every sworn obligation of self-denial may be upheld by her husband or annulled by her husband.
30.15: If her husband offers no objection from that day to the next, he has upheld all the vows or obligations she has assumed: he has upheld them by offering no objection on the day he found out.
30.16: But if he annuls them after the day he finds out, he shall bear her guilt.
30.17: Those are the laws that GOD enjoined upon Moses between a husband and his wife, and as between a father and his daughter while in her father’s household by reason of her youth.

31.2: “Avenge the Israelite people on the Midianites; then you shall be gathered to your kin.”
31.3: Moses spoke to the people, saying, “Let troops be picked out from among you for a campaign, and let them fall upon Midian to wreak GOD’s vengeance on Midian.
31.4: You shall dispatch on the campaign a thousand from every one of the tribes of Israel.”
31.5: So a thousand from each tribe were furnished from the divisions of Israel, twelve thousand picked for the campaign.
31.6: Moses dispatched them on the campaign, a thousand from each tribe, with Phinehas son of Eleazar serving as a priest on the campaign, equipped with the sacred utensils and the trumpets for sounding the blasts.
31.7: They took the field against Midian, as GOD had commanded Moses, and slew every male.
31.8: Along with their other victims, they slew the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also put Balaam son of Beor to the sword.
31.9: The Israelites took the women and other noncombatants of the Midianites captive, and seized as booty all their beasts, all their herds, and all their wealth.
31.10: And they destroyed by fire all the towns in which they were settled, and their encampments.
31.11: They gathered all the spoil and all the booty, human and animal
31.12: And they brought the captives, the booty, and the spoil to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the whole Israelite community, at the camp in the steppes of Moab, at the Jordan near Jericho.
31.13: Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the chieftains of the community came out to meet them outside the camp.
31.14: Moses became angry with the commanders of the army, the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds, who had come back from the military campaign.
31.15: Moses said to them, “You have spared every female!
31.16: Yet they are the very ones who, at the bidding of Balaam, induced…limsor uncertain. the Israelites to trespass against GOD in the matter of Peor, so that GOD’s community was struck by the plague.
31.17: Now, therefore, slay every male among the noncombatants, and slay also every woman who has known a man carnally
31.18: But spare every female noncombatant who has not had carnal relations with a man.
31.19: “You shall then stay outside the camp seven days; every one among you or among your captives who has slain a person or touched a corpse shall cleanse himself on the third and seventh days.
31.20: You shall also cleanse every cloth, every article of skin, everything made of goats’ hair, and every object of wood.”
31.21: Eleazar the priest said to the troops who had taken part in the fighting, “This is the ritual law that GOD has enjoined upon Moses
31.22: Gold and silver, copper, iron, tin, and lead
31.23: Any article that can withstand fire—these you shall pass through fire and they shall be pure, except that they must be cleansed with water of lustration; and anything that cannot withstand fire you must pass through water.
31.24: On the seventh day you shall wash your clothes and be pure, and after that you may enter the camp.”
31.26: “You and Eleazar the priest and the family heads of the community take an inventory of the booty that was captured, human and animal
31.27: And divide the booty equally between the combatants who engaged in the campaign and the rest of the community.
31.28: You shall exact a levy for GOD: in the case of the warriors who engaged in the campaign, one item in five hundred, of persons, oxen, donkeys, and sheep
31.29: Shall be taken from their half-share and given to Eleazar the priest as a contribution to GOD
31.30: And from the half-share of the other Israelites you shall withhold one in every fifty human beings as well as cattle, donkeys, and sheep—all the animals—and give them to the Levites, who attend to the duties of GOD’s Tabernacle.”
31.31: Moses and Eleazar the priest did as GOD commanded Moses.
31.32: The amount of booty, other than the spoil that the troops had plundered, came to 675,000 sheep
31.35: And a total of 32,000 human beings, namely, the females who had not had carnal relations.
31.36: Thus, the half-share of those who had engaged in the campaign was as follows: The number of sheep was 337
31.37: And GOD’s levy from the sheep was
31.38: The cattle came to 36,000, from which GOD’s levy was
31.39: The donkeys came to 30,500, from which GOD’s levy was 61.
31.40: And the number of human beings was 16,000, from which GOD’s levy was 32.
31.41: Moses gave the contributions levied for GOD to Eleazar the priest, as GOD had commanded Moses.
31.42: As for the half-share of the other Israelites, which Moses withdrew from those who had taken the field
31.43: That half-share of the community consisted of 337,500 sheep
31.47: From this half-share of the Israelites, Moses withheld one in every fifty humans and animals; and he gave them to the Levites, who attended to the duties of GOD’s Tabernacle, as GOD had commanded Moses.
31.48: The commanders of the troop divisions, the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds, approached Moses.
31.49: They said to Moses, “Your servants have made a check of the warriors in our charge, and not one of us is missing.
31.50: So we have brought as an offering to GOD such articles of gold as each of us came upon: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and pendants, uncertain; cf. Exod. 35.22. that expiation may be made for our persons before GOD.”
31.51: Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted the gold from them, all kinds of wrought articles.
31.52: All the gold that was offered by the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds as a contribution to GOD came to 16,750 shekels.
31.53: But in the ranks, everyone kept his booty for himself.
31.54: So Moses and Eleazar the priest accepted the gold from the officers of thousands and the officers of hundreds and brought it to the Tent of Meeting, as a reminder in behalf of the Israelites before GOD.

32.1: The Reubenites and the Gadites owned cattle in very great numbers. Noting that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were a region suitable for cattle
32.2: The Gadites and the Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the chieftains of the community, and said
32.3: “Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon
32.4: The land that GOD has conquered for the community of Israel—is cattle country, and your servants have cattle.
32.5: It would be a favor to us,” they continued, “if this land were given to your servants as a holding; do not move us across the Jordan.”
32.6: Moses replied to the Gadites and the Reubenites, “Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here?
32.7: Why will you turn the minds of the Israelites from crossing into the land that GOD has given them?
32.8: That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to survey the land.
32.9: After going up to the wadi Eshcol and surveying the land, they turned the minds of the Israelites from invading the land that GOD had given them.
32.10: Thereupon GOD was incensed and swore
32.11: ‘None of those involved from twenty years up who came out of Egypt shall see the land that I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, for they did not remain loyal to Me
32.12: None except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, for they remained loyal to GOD.’
32.13: Incensed at Israel, GOD made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had provoked GOD’s displeasure was gone.
32.14: And now you, a breed of sinful men, have replaced your fathers, to add still further to GOD’s wrath against Israel.
32.15: If you turn away from God, who then abandons them once more in the wilderness, you will bring calamity upon all this people.”
32.16: Then they stepped up to him and said, “We will build here sheepfolds for our flocks and towns for our dependents.
32.17: And we will hasten uncertain. as shock-troops in the van of the Israelites until we have established them in their home, while our dependents stay in the fortified towns because of the inhabitants of the land.
32.18: We will not return to our homes until the other Israelites are in possession of their portion.
32.19: But we will not have a share with them in the territory beyond the Jordan, for we have received our share on the east side of the Jordan.”
32.20: Moses said to them, “If you do this, if at the instance of GOD you go to battle as shock-troops
32.21: And at the instance of GOD every shock-fighter among you crosses the Jordan, until God has directly dispossessed the enemies
32.22: And the land has been subdued at the instance of GOD, and then you return—you shall be clear before GOD and before Israel; and this land shall be your holding under GOD.
32.23: But if you do not do so, you will have sinned against GOD; and know that your sin will overtake you.
32.24: Build towns for your children and sheepfolds for your flocks, but do what you have promised.”
32.25: The Gadites and the Reubenites answered Moses, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
32.26: Our children, our wives, our flocks, and all our other livestock will stay behind in the towns of Gilead
32.27: While your servants, all those recruited for war, cross over at the instance of GOD, to engage in battle—as my lord orders.”
32.28: Then Moses gave instructions concerning them to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the family heads of the Israelite tribes.
32.29: Moses said to them, “If every shock-fighter among the Gadites and the Reubenites crosses the Jordan with you to do battle at the instance of GOD, and the land is subdued before you, you shall give them the land of Gilead as a holding.
32.30: But if they do not cross over with you as shock-troops, they shall receive holdings among you in the land of Canaan.”
32.31: The Gadites and the Reubenites said in reply, “Whatever GOD has spoken concerning your servants, that we will do.
32.32: We ourselves will cross over as shock-troops, at the instance of GOD, into the land of Canaan; and we shall keep our hereditary holding across the Jordan.”
32.33: So Moses assigned to them—to the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph—the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of King Og of Bashan, the land with its various cities and the territories of their surrounding towns.
32.34: The Gadites rebuilt Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer
32.36: Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran as fortified towns or as enclosures for flocks.
32.37: The Reubenites rebuilt Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim
32.38: Nebo, Baal-meon—some names being changed—and Sibmah; they gave their own names to towns that they rebuilt.
32.39: The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, dispossessing the Amorites who were there
32.40: So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
32.41: Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages, which he renamed Havvoth-jair.
32.42: And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its dependencies, renaming it Nobah after himself.

33.1: These were the marches of the Israelites who started out from the land of Egypt, troop by troop, in the charge of Moses and Aaron.
33.2: Moses recorded the starting points of their various marches as directed by GOD. Their marches, by starting points, were as follows
33.3: They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. It was on the morrow of the passover offering that the Israelites started out defiantly, in plain view of all the Egyptians.
33.4: The Egyptians meanwhile were burying those among them whom GOD had struck down, every male first-born—whereby GOD executed judgment on their gods.
33.5: The Israelites set out from Rameses and encamped at Succoth.
33.6: They set out from Succoth and encamped at Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
33.7: They set out from Etham and turned about toward Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they encamped before Migdol.
33.8: They set out from Pene-hahiroth and passed through the sea into the wilderness; and they made a three-days’ journey in the wilderness of Etham and encamped at Marah.
33.9: They set out from Marah and came to Elim. There were twelve springs in Elim and seventy palm trees, so they encamped there.
33.10: They set out from Elim and encamped by the Sea of Reeds.
33.11: They set out from the Sea of Reeds and encamped in the wilderness of Sin.
33.12: They set out from the wilderness of Sin and encamped at Dophkah.
33.13: They set out from Dophkah and encamped at Alush.
33.14: They set out from Alush and encamped at Rephidim; it was there that the people had no water to drink.
33.15: They set out from Rephidim and encamped in the wilderness of Sinai.
33.16: They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and encamped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
33.17: They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and encamped at Hazeroth.
33.18: They set out from Hazeroth and encamped at Rithmah.
33.19: They set out from Rithmah and encamped at Rimmon-perez.
33.20: They set out from Rimmon-perez and encamped at Libnah.
33.21: They set out from Libnah and encamped at Rissah.
33.22: They set out from Rissah and encamped at Kehelath.
33.23: They set out from Kehelath and encamped at Mount Shepher.
33.24: They set out from Mount Shepher and encamped at Haradah.
33.25: They set out from Haradah and encamped at Makheloth.
33.26: They set out from Makheloth and encamped at Tahath.
33.27: They set out from Tahath and encamped at Terah.
33.28: They set out from Terah and encamped at Mithkah.
33.29: They set out from Mithkah and encamped at Hashmonah.
33.30: They set out from Hashmonah and encamped at Moseroth.
33.31: They set out from Moseroth and encamped at Bene-jaakan.
33.32: They set out from Bene-jaakan and encamped at Hor-haggidgad.
33.33: They set out from Hor-haggidgad and encamped at Jotbath.
33.34: They set out from Jotbath and encamped at Abronah.
33.35: They set out from Abronah and encamped at Ezion-geber.
33.36: They set out from Ezion-geber and encamped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
33.37: They set out from Kadesh and encamped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
33.38: Aaron the priest ascended Mount Hor at GOD’s command and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites had left the land of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
33.39: Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
33.40: And the Canaanite, king of Arad, who dwelt in the Negeb, in the land of Canaan, learned of the coming of the Israelites.
33.41: They set out from Mount Hor and encamped at Zalmonah.
33.42: They set out from Zalmonah and encamped at Punon.
33.43: They set out from Punon and encamped at Oboth.
33.44: They set out from Oboth and encamped at Iye-abarim, in the territory of Moab.
33.45: They set out from Iyim and encamped at Dibon-gad.
33.46: They set out from Dibon-gad and encamped at Almon-diblathaim.
33.47: They set out from Almon-diblathaim and encamped in the hills of Abarim, before Nebo.
33.48: They set out from the hills of Abarim and encamped in the steppes of Moab, at the Jordan near Jericho
33.49: They encamped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the steppes of Moab.
33.50: In the steppes of Moab, at the Jordan near Jericho, GOD spoke to Moses, saying
33.51: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan
33.52: You shall dispossess all the inhabitants of the land; you shall destroy all their figured uncertain; cf. Lev. 26.1. objects; you shall destroy all their molten images, and you shall demolish all their cult places.
33.53: And you shall take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have assigned the land to you to possess.
33.54: You shall apportion the land among yourselves by lot, clan by clan: with larger groups increase the share, with smaller groups reduce the share. Wherever the lot falls for it, that shall be its location. You shall have your portions according to your ancestral tribes.
33.55: But if you do not dispossess the inhabitants of the land, those whom you allow to remain shall be stings in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they shall harass you in the land in which you live
33.56: So that I will do to you what I planned to do to them.

34.2: Instruct the Israelite people and say to them: When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that shall fall to you as your portion, the land of Canaan with its various boundaries
34.3: Your southern sector shall extend from the wilderness of Zin alongside Edom. Your southern boundary shall start on the east from the tip of the Dead Sea.
34.4: Your boundary shall then turn to pass south of the ascent of Akrabbim and continue to Zin, and its limits shall be south of Kadesh-barnea, reaching Hazar-addar and continuing to Azmon.
34.5: From Azmon the boundary shall turn toward the Wadi of Egypt and terminate at the Sea.
34.6: For the western boundary you shall have the coast of the Great Sea; that shall serve as your western boundary.
34.7: This shall be your northern boundary: Draw a line from the Great Sea to Mount Hor
34.8: From Mount Hor draw a line to Lebo-hamath, and let the boundary reach Zedad.
34.9: The boundary shall then run to Ziphron and terminate at Hazar-enan. That shall be your northern boundary.
34.10: For your eastern boundary you shall draw a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
34.11: From Shepham the boundary shall descend to Riblah on the east side of Ain; from there the boundary shall continue downward and abut on the eastern slopes of the Sea of Chinnereth.
34.12: The boundary shall then descend along the Jordan and terminate at the Dead Sea. That shall be your land as defined by its boundaries on all sides.
34.13: Moses instructed the Israelites, saying: This is the land you are to receive by lot as your hereditary portion, which GOD has commanded to be given to the nine and a half tribes.
34.14: For the Reubenite tribe by its ancestral houses, the Gadite tribe by its ancestral houses, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their portions
34.15: Those two and a half tribes have received their portions across the Jordan, opposite Jericho, on the east, the orient side.
34.17: These are the names of the men through whom the land shall be apportioned for you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
34.18: You shall also take a chieftain from each tribe through whom the land shall be apportioned
34.19: And these are their names: From the tribe of Judah: Caleb son of Jephunneh.
34.20: From the Simeonite tribe: Samuel son of Ammihud.
34.21: From the tribe of Benjamin: Elidad son of Chislon.
34.22: From the Danite tribe: a chieftain, Bukki son of Jogli.
34.23: For the descendants of Joseph: from the Manassite tribe: a chieftain, Hanniel son of Ephod
34.24: And from the Ephraimite tribe: a chieftain, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
34.25: From the Zebulunite tribe: a chieftain, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
34.26: From the Issacharite tribe: a chieftain, Paltiel son of Azzan.
34.27: From the Asherite tribe: a chieftain, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
34.28: From the Naphtalite tribe: a chieftain, Pedahel son of Ammihud.
34.29: It was these whom GOD designated to allot portions to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.

35.1: GOD spoke to Moses in the steppes of Moab at the Jordan near Jericho, saying
35.2: Instruct the Israelite people to assign, out of the holdings apportioned to them, towns for the Levites to dwell in; you shall also assign to the Levites pasture land around their towns.
35.3: The towns shall be theirs to dwell in, and the pasture shall be for the cattle they own and all their other animals.
35.4: The town pasture that you are to assign to the Levites shall extend a thousand cubits outside the town wall all around.
35.5: You shall measure off two thousand cubits outside the town on the east side, two thousand on the south side, two thousand on the west side, and two thousand on the north side, with the town in the center. That shall be the pasture for their towns.
35.6: The towns that you assign to the Levites shall comprise the six cities of refuge that you are to designate for a manslayer to flee to, to which you shall add forty-two towns.
35.7: Thus the total of the towns that you assign to the Levites shall be forty-eight towns, with their pasture.
35.8: In assigning towns from the holdings of the Israelites, take more from the larger groups and less from the smaller, so that each assigns towns to the Levites in proportion to the share it receives.
35.10: Speak to the Israelite people and say to them: When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan
35.11: You shall provide yourselves with places to serve you as cities of refuge to which a manslayer who has slain a person unintentionally may flee.
35.12: The cities shall serve you as a refuge from the avenger, so that the manslayer may not die unless there is a trial before the assembly.
35.13: The towns that you thus assign shall be six cities of refuge in all.
35.14: Three cities shall be designated beyond the Jordan, and the other three shall be designated in the land of Canaan: they shall serve as cities of refuge.
35.15: These six cities shall serve the Israelites and the resident aliens among them for refuge, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
35.16: Anyone, however, who strikes another with an iron object so that death results is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
35.17: If one struck another with a stone tool that could cause death, and death resulted, that person is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
35.18: Similarly, if one struck another with a wooden tool that could cause death, and death resulted, that person is a murderer; the murderer must be put to death.
35.19: It is the blood-avenger who shall put the murderer to death; that is who shall put them to death upon encounter.
35.20: So, too, if one pushed another in hate or hurled something at them on purpose and death resulted
35.21: Or if one struck with their hand in enmity and death resulted, the assailant shall be put to death; that person is a murderer. The blood-avenger shall put the murderer to death upon encounter.
35.22: But if the person pushed them without malice aforethought or hurled any object at them unintentionally
35.23: Or inadvertently dropped upon them any deadly object of stone, and death resulted—though not being an enemy and not seeking to harm
35.24: In such cases the assembly shall decide between the slayer and the blood-avenger.
35.25: The assembly shall protect the manslayer from the blood-avenger, and the assembly shall restore the former to the same city of refuge, and there he shall remain until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the sacred oil.
35.26: But if the manslayer ever goes outside the limits of that city of refuge
35.27: And is found by the blood-avenger outside the limits of the city of refuge, and if the blood-avenger kills the manslayer, there is no bloodguilt on that account.
35.28: For the slayer must remain inside the city of refuge until the death of the high priest; after the death of the high priest, the manslayer may return home.
35.29: Such shall be your law of procedure throughout the ages in all your settlements.
35.30: If anyone slays a person, the manslayer may be executed only on the evidence of witnesses; the testimony of a single witness against a person shall not suffice for a sentence of death.
35.31: You may not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of a capital crime; a murderer must be put to death.
35.32: Nor may you accept ransom in lieu of flight to a city of refuge, enabling someone to return home before the death of the priest.
35.33: You shall not pollute the land in which you live; for blood pollutes the land, and the land can have no expiation for blood that is shed on it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
35.34: You shall not defile the land in which you live, in which I Myself abide, for I GOD abide among the Israelite people.

36.1: The family heads in the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir son of Manasseh, one of the Josephite clans, came forward and appealed to Moses and the chieftains, family heads of the Israelites.
36.2: They said, “GOD commanded my lord to assign the land to the Israelites as shares by lot, and my lord was further commanded by GOD to assign the share of our kinsman Zelophehad to his daughters.
36.3: Now, if they become the wives of persons from another Israelite tribe, their share will be cut off from our ancestral portion and be added to the portion of the tribe into which they marry; thus our allotted portion will be diminished.
36.4: And even when the Israelites observe the jubilee, their share will be added to that of the tribe into which they marry, and their share will be cut off from the ancestral portion of our tribe.”
36.5: So Moses, at GOD’s bidding, instructed the Israelites, saying: “The plea of the Josephite tribe is just.
36.6: This is what GOD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may become the wives of anyone they wish, provided they marry into a clan of their father’s tribe.
36.7: No inheritance of the Israelites may pass over from one tribe to another, but the Israelite heirs—each of them—must remain bound to the ancestral portion of their tribe.
36.8: Every daughter among the Israelite tribes who inherits a share must become the wife of someone from a clan of her father’s tribe, in order that every Israelite heir may keep an ancestral share.
36.9: Thus no inheritance shall pass over from one tribe to another, but the Israelite tribes shall remain bound each to its portion.”
36.10: The daughters of Zelophehad did as GOD had commanded Moses
36.11: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, Zelophehad’s daughters, became the wives of their uncles’ sons
36.12: Marrying into clans of descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph; and so their share remained in the tribe of their father’s clan.
36.13: These are the commandments and regulations that GOD enjoined upon the Israelites, through Moses, on the steppes of Moab, at the Jordan near Jericho.

1.1: These are the words that Moses addressed to all Israel on the other side of the Jordan.—Through the wilderness, in the Arabah near Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Di-zahab
1.2: It is eleven days from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the Mount Seir route.
1.3: It was in the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, that Moses addressed the Israelites in accordance with the instructions that GOD had given him for them
1.4: After he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and King Og of Bashan, who dwelt at Ashtaroth and Edrei.
1.5: On the other side of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses undertook to expound this Teaching. He said
1.6: The ETERNAL our God spoke to us at Horeb, saying: You have stayed long enough at this mountain.
